mainTopic: What does 'a period of fitness' in the מעילה משנה mean, when does a פסול make the blood שיריים, and what does a פיגול sprinkling do to מעילה?
overview: The גמרא wants to know what 'a period of fitness' in our משנה means: fitness to sprinkle the blood, or fitness to eat the meat. First it suggests our משנה's wording is not exact, like a similar משנה in זבחים. רב אסי objects that two משניות would not both use loose wording, so the גמרא decides our משנה about מעילה is exact. The זבחים wording instead teaches that when a פסול receives and sprinkles, the rest of the blood becomes שיריים (leftovers). The גמרא then challenges this from רבי יוחנן, who said only sprinkling with פיגול intent makes שיריים. It answers that רבי יוחנן's list covers only things invalid for the ציבור. A טמא, who can serve for the ציבור, does make שיריים, while other פסולין do not. Finally, the גמרא tries to prove the 'fitness to sprinkle' reading from a ברייתא that says פיגול is always subject to מעילה. It rejects that proof: the ברייתא may be speaking after sprinkling, and 'always' teaches רב גידל's rule that a פיגול sprinkling neither takes an offering out of מעילה nor brings it in.

steps.title: Maybe our משנה is not exact either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that, just like the משנה in זבחים, our משנה's wording 'פסולין received and sprinkled' is not meant exactly, so we cannot learn anything from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too here, the wording is not exact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the inference people wanted to draw from our משנה's wording. It says our משנה, like the one in זבחים, may not be precise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone wanted to learn from the words 'פסולין received' that only an unfit קבלה makes מעילה apply, which would mean שעת הכשר is about sprinkling. If the wording is לאו דוקא, the same law would apply even when fit people received and unfit people sprinkled. Then there is no proof, and שעת הכשר could mean fitness for eating.

keyTerms.meaning: So too / here as well
Not exact; the wording is not meant precisely
A time when the offering was fit (the phrase being defined in this סוגיא)

phrases.english: So too here, it is not exact.
phrases.notes: He means our מעילה משנה, compared with the זבחים משנה about a חטאת that the גמרא just mentioned as not exact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from the previous section: it applies the 'not exact' reading of the זבחים משנה to our משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the attempt to learn the meaning of שעת הכשר from the exact wording of our משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the wording 'פסולין received and sprinkled' is exact. But a parallel משנה uses the same wording loosely.

steps.title: Why would two משניות both be inexact?
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי objects: if the wording is loose in both places, why would the תנא teach two משניות that way?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: If so, why do I need the משנה to teach two such cases?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי challenges the idea that our משנה is also inexact. It is hard to believe the same loose wording would appear in two separate משניות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One loose phrase can be explained, but repeating it in two places suggests at least one of them is exact on purpose. So at least one משנה must be teaching something by using that exact wording.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if what you said is true
Why do I need it? (asking what purpose something serves)
To teach two (cases or משניות)

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, לְמָה לִי לְמִיתְנֵי תַּרְתֵּי?
phrases.english: If so, why do I need it to teach two?
phrases.notes: The 'two' are our משנה here in מעילה and the משנה in זבחים, which use the same wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: אם כן, למה לי למיתני תרתי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggestion in step 1 that our משנה is לאו דוקא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that both משניות are inexact.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תנא would not use the same loose wording twice for no reason. So at least one of the משניות must mean it exactly.

steps.title: Our מעילה משנה is exact after all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back and says that the משנה about מעילה really is exact.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really, the משנה about מעילה is exact.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of רב אסי's question, the גמרא drops the 'not exact' idea for our משנה and says its wording is precise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If our משנה is exact, then מעילה applies only when פסולין did the קבלה. If fit people received the blood, the offering had a time of fitness for sprinkling. So שעת הכשר means fitness for זריקה, not for eating. The next step explains why the זבחים משנה uses the same wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (dropping the previous idea)
Really / actually (going back to an earlier position)
Misuse of consecrated (הקדש) property

steps.whyThisMatters: On this reading, שעת הכשר in our משנה means fitness for sprinkling the blood. Later the גמרא tries again to prove this from a ברייתא (steps 10–14).

phrases.english: Rather, actually, the one about misuse is exact,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אסי by saying only one משנה (זבחים) is loose, while ours is exact.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the loose wording to only one of the two משניות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our מעילה משנה is exact, so שעת הכשר refers to fitness for sprinkling.

steps.title: What the זבחים משנה is really teaching
steps.stepSummary: The זבחים משנה mentions 'פסולין received and sprinkled' to teach that blood sprinkled by a פסול makes the rest of the blood into שיריים. So a fit כהן who receives and sprinkles afterward accomplishes nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what it teaches us: a פסול makes the blood into leftovers. So even though an unfit person received and sprinkled, and then a fit person received and sprinkled, it counts for nothing. Why? Because it is leftover blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the זבחים משנה, which is not exact, still uses the words 'פסולין received.' Those words teach a separate new law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an unfit person receives and sprinkles the blood, that sprinkling turns the rest of the blood into שיריים, as if a proper sprinkling had already happened. So if a fit כהן later receives blood in a second vessel and sprinkles it, that sprinkling does not count. This explains the wording of זבחים without making two משניות loose for no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it comes to teach us
Someone unfit for Temple service
Leftover blood after the required sprinkling; it no longer counts for the service
Fit (for Temple service)
It is nothing; it does not count at all
What is the reason?

steps.whatToRemember: Our מעילה משנה is exact, so שעת הכשר means fitness for sprinkling. The זבחים משנה says 'פסולין received' to teach that when a פסול receives and sprinkles, the remaining blood becomes שיריים.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the fit כהן's sprinkling counts because he himself is fit. The blood he used was already 'leftovers' because the פסול had already sprinkled.

phrases.english: And this is what it teaches us:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the משנה in זבחים, the one that really is loose in its wording.

phrases.english: that an unfit person makes leftovers,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּקִיבֵּל פָּסוּל וְזָרַק,
phrases.english: even though an unfit one received and sprinkled,
phrases.notes: Picture the blood in two vessels: the unfit one handles the first vessel, and the fit one handles the second.

phrases.english: and a fit one received and sprinkled –
it is nothing.
What is the reason? Because they are leftovers.

steps.triggerLanguage: והא קא משמע לן: דפסול עושה שירים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to רב אסי by giving a reason for the wording of the זבחים משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the loose-wording משנה a separate teaching, so the repeated wording is explained.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The זבחים wording would have no purpose if it is not exact.
steps.terutzMaskana: The זבחים wording teaches that a פסול makes the blood שיריים, so a later fit sprinkling is worthless.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Our מעילה משנה is precise, and the זבחים משנה teaches פסול עושה שיריים.

steps.title: A challenge from ריש לקיש's question to רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes an exchange between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן. It seems to say that only פיגול intent, not a פסול, creates שיריים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't ריש לקיש ask רבי יוחנן: if a פסול sprinkled, does he turn the rest of the blood into שיריים? And רבי יוחנן answered: nothing makes שיריים except sprinkling with intent for outside its time or outside its place, because those sprinklings count enough to make the offering פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that seems to go against what it just said in step 4. This step lays out the source, and the next step spells out exactly how it contradicts step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said a פסול's handling of the blood turns the rest into שיריים. רבי יוחנן says only a sprinkling with פיגול intent (חוץ לזמנו or חוץ למקומו) does that. The reason is that such a sprinkling is 'strong' enough to make the meat פיגול, so it also counts as a real sprinkling for this purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Intent to eat the offering after its allowed time
Intent to eat the offering outside its allowed place
The sprinkling 'works' enough to make the offering פיגול

steps.confusionAlert: חוץ לזמנו and חוץ למקומו here do not mean the כהן actually did something late or in the wrong place. They mean he sprinkled while intending that the meat be eaten at the wrong time or place.

phrases.english: But didn't he ask of him
Reish Lakish of Rabbi Yochanan:
An unfit person, what is the law, does he make leftovers?
phrases.notes: He means: if a פסול sprinkled some of the blood, does the rest now count as leftovers?

phrases.english: And he said to him:
You have nothing that makes leftovers
except outside its time and outside its place,
since they effect acceptance for making it piggul.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside source that seems to clash with step 4's claim that a פסול makes שיריים.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 4's claim that a פסול who receives and sprinkles turns the rest of the blood into שיריים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן limits the making of שיריים to sprinkling with פיגול intent, which seems to leave out a פסול.

steps.title: Reading רבי יוחנן as leaving out a פסול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the challenge. Doesn't רבי יוחנן's answer mean that a פסול does not make שיריים?
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it that he means: but not a פסול?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states plainly how the quote from step 5 contradicts step 4. רבי יוחנן seems to be excluding a פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only פיגול intent makes שיריים, then a פסול's sprinkling would not. That goes directly against step 4, which said a פסול does make the rest of the blood שיריים.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? (a way to suggest a reading)
Except for, leaving out

phrases.english: What, is it not to the exclusion of an unfit person?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge by drawing the conclusion from the quote in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 4's ruling that a פסול makes שיריים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The quote limits שיריים to פיגול intent, so a פסול must be left out.

steps.title: Maybe a פסול is included too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: no, a פסול also makes שיריים.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, even a פסול makes שיריים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reading from step 6. It suggests that רבי יוחנן was not excluding a פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tries to save step 4. It suggests רבי יוחנן's list was only about invalid intent, and a פסול also creates שיריים. If so, there is no clash with step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: Even

phrases.english: No, even an unfit person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers by rejecting the inference made in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference that רבי יוחנן excluded a פסול.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes רבי יוחנן's list was meant to leave out a פסול, but it may include one.

steps.title: But רבי יוחנן said 'you have nothing except'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the defense. The words 'אין לך', 'you have nothing except', sound like a complete list, so a פסול cannot be included.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he taught 'you have nothing except'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 7 by pointing to the exact words רבי יוחנן used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אין לך... אלא' means 'nothing at all, except these.' That is a closed list: only חוץ לזמנו and חוץ למקומו. So it is hard to say a פסול is also included, and the problem from step 6 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: You have nothing (a phrase that signals a complete, closed list)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא reads a sage's words closely. A phrase like 'אין לך' carries legal weight because it shuts out anything not mentioned.

phrases.english: But he taught 'you do not have'!
phrases.notes: He is pointing back to רבי יוחנן's words in step 5: 'you have nothing that makes leftovers except...'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 7's defense using the wording of the quote in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 7's claim that a פסול is also included in רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'אין לך... אלא' makes a closed list, so nothing outside פיגול intent, including a פסול, can make שיריים.

steps.title: Rereading 'You have nothing except': an impure כהן is not on the list
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's list covers only invalid services that do not work for the ציבור yet still make שיריים, which are חוץ לזמנו and חוץ למקומו. A טמא, who is valid for the ציבור, does make שיריים. Other פסולין do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: the only things that are not valid for the community and still turn the blood into leftovers are 'beyond its time' and 'outside its place.' An impure כהן is valid for the community, so he does turn the blood into leftovers. Other disqualified people are not valid for the community, and they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 8. It explains that the 'complete list' in רבי יוחנן's words is a narrower list than we thought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 argued that 'אין לך' is a full list, so no פסול can make שיריים. The answer is that the list only covers services that are invalid even for the ציבור. A טמא was never meant to be on it, because טומאה is allowed for the ציבור. So the earlier claim that a פסול makes שיריים holds only for a טמא, and other פסולין like a blemished כהן do not make שיריים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it is teaching': the גמרא is reinterpreting a statement
Effects acceptance, meaning the service works for the owner
For the community, in communal offerings
A ritually impure כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוחנן is saying a טמא is worse than other פסולין. The point is the opposite: because a טמא can be valid for the ציבור, his service counts enough to make the blood into שיריים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reading settles that only a טמא, among the regular פסולין, makes the blood שיריים. That fits the earlier reading of the זבחים משנה from Step 4.

phrases.english: This is what he is teaching:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְרַצֶּה בְּצִיבּוּר
phrases.english: You have nothing that does not effect acceptance for the community
and yet makes the blood leftovers
except beyond its time and outside its place.
But an impure one, who is valid for the community,
phrases.notes: An impure כהן may serve for the community when most of the community is impure.

phrases.english: does make the blood leftovers.
Other disqualified ones
who are not valid for the community
do not make the blood leftovers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8's claim that 'אין לך' is a complete list that rules out every פסול.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of a statement: the list covers only things invalid for the ציבור.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אין לך' seemed to say that only פיגול-type intent ever makes שיריים, so no פסול could.
steps.terutzMaskana: A טמא, who is valid for the ציבור, makes שיריים. Other פסולין do not.

steps.title: A ברייתא: there is always מעילה with פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a source saying that פיגול always carries liability for מעילה. It is setting up a proof about the משנה's phrase 'a period of fitness for the כהנים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: with פיגול, a person is always liable for misusing it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question about the משנה and quotes a ברייתא. This line is a setup; the proof itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע in the משנה says there is no more מעילה once the offering had a period of fitness for the כהנים. The question is whether that means fitness to sprinkle the blood or fitness to eat the meat. The ברייתא tells us that פיגול never leaves מעילה. Next, the גמרא will ask which case the ברייתא is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering ruined by the intent to eat it after its proper time
Liable for מְעִילָה, misusing holy property
Always, in every situation

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Piggul: one is always liable for misuse with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שיריים discussion and turns to the meaning of רבי יהושע's phrase in the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The meaning of 'שעת הכושר לכהנים' in the משנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: הפיגול לעולם מועלין בו

steps.title: The inference: fitness for sprinkling is what the משנה means
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא is talking about a case where the blood was not yet sprinkled, then only פיגול keeps the מעילה. Blood collected properly, and ready to be sprinkled, would already end it. So the משנה means היתר זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it talking about a case where he did not sprinkle yet? Then learn from it that the משנה means fitness for sprinkling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof from the ברייתא. It concludes that 'a period of fitness' in the משנה means the blood was ready to be sprinkled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the כהן received the blood but did not sprinkle it. The ברייתא says there is still מעילה only because of the פיגול. That implies a normal offering in the same state, with its blood just ready to sprinkle, already leaves מעילה. So being ready for זריקה is enough, which shows the משנה is about היתר זריקה and not היתר אכילה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is it not...?': introduces a suggested reading of the case
Sprinkling or throwing the blood on the מזבח
The point when the blood is fit to be sprinkled
'Learn from it': draws a conclusion

steps.confusionAlert: The point is not about פיגול itself. The proof comes from what the ברייתא implies about a normal, non-פיגול offering in the same state.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof held, it would decide when an offering stops carrying מעילה: once its blood is fit to be sprinkled, not only once the meat may be eaten. The next step questions whether the proof really works.

phrases.english: Is it not where he did not sprinkle?
And learn from it:
Fitness for sprinkling is what we learned!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof out of the ברייתא quoted in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That 'שעת הכושר לכהנים' in the משנה means היתר זריקה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The implied contrast in 'הפיגול לעולם מועלין בו' when read as a case where the blood was not sprinkled

steps.title: No proof: the ברייתא may be after sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא could be talking about a case where the blood was already sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The ברייתא could be talking about a case where he already sprinkled the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 11. It says the ברייתא could be talking about a case where the blood was already sprinkled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blood was already sprinkled, the ברייתא is teaching that a פיגול sprinkling does not end מעילה, while a proper sprinkling would. That fits the view that the משנה means היתר אכילה, permission to eat the meat after a proper sprinkling. So the ברייתא does not prove that the משנה means היתר זריקה.

keyTerms.meaning: He sprinkled it, meaning the blood was already sprinkled
Permission to eat the meat, which comes after a proper sprinkling

phrases.english: No, he sprinkled it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 11's reading of the ברייתא as talking about before the sprinkling.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that the משנה's 'period of fitness' means היתר זריקה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Step 11 assumed the ברייתא spoke before sprinkling. It can just as well speak after a פיגול sprinkling, which fits the היתר אכילה reading.

steps.title: What does 'always' add?
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא is after sprinkling, the גמרא asks what the word 'לעולם' (always) is teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on its own new reading. If the case is after sprinkling, why does the ברייתא say פיגול is 'always' subject to מעילה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לעולם' sounds like it adds something beyond the basic rule. On the new reading, the גמרא must find what that extra teaching is. This sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Always; the ברייתא's word saying פיגול is always subject to מעילה

phrases.english: And what is 'always'?
phrases.notes: This is the word in the ברייתא from step 10: one 'always' commits מעילה with פיגול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests step 12's new reading against the ברייתא's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the ברייתא speaks after sprinkling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the case is simply after sprinkling, the word 'לעולם' seems to add nothing, so it needs an explanation.

steps.title: 'Always' teaches רב גידל's rule
steps.stepSummary: 'Always' teaches רב גידל's rule: sprinkling פיגול blood neither takes an offering out of מעילה nor brings it into מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us like רב גידל. רב גידל said in the name of רב: sprinkling the blood of a פיגול offering does not take it out of מעילה, and it does not bring it into מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'always' points to רב גידל's rule. A פיגול sprinkling has no effect on מעילה either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For קדשי קדשים, a proper sprinkling would end מעילה, but a פיגול sprinkling does not, so מעילה stays. For קדשים קלים, a proper sprinkling would make the אימורים subject to מעילה, but a פיגול sprinkling does not. 'Always' means the פיגול sprinkling never changes the מעילה status, so the reading from step 12 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the blood with a פיגול intent
Takes the offering out of the rules of מעילה
Brings something into the rules of מעילה
Offerings of the most holy level
Offerings of a lesser holiness

steps.whatToRemember: A פיגול sprinkling does nothing to מעילה: it does not take קדשי קדשים out, and it does not bring the אימורים of קדשים קלים in. So the ברייתא gives no proof that the משנה means היתר זריקה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a פיגול sprinkling counts as a real sprinkling for מעילה. It counts for neither direction.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains the ברייתא's word 'always' in a way that fits the היתר אכילה reading, so the question about the משנה's meaning stays open.

phrases.aramaic: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן כִּדְרַב גִּידֵּל,
phrases.english: This teaches us like רב גידל,
as רב גידל said in the name of רב:

phrases.aramaic: זְרִיקַת פִּיגּוּל – אֵינוֹ מוֹצִיא מִידֵי מְעִילָה,
phrases.english: Sprinkling of פיגול does not take it out of מעילה,
phrases.notes: This is about קדשי קדשים, which a proper sprinkling would take out of מעילה.

phrases.english: and does not bring it into מעילה.
phrases.notes: This is about the אימורים of קדשים קלים, which only become subject to מעילה after a proper sprinkling.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן כִּדְרַב גִּידֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 by giving 'always' its own teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra word its own legal meaning by tying it to an existing rule (רב גידל).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought 'always' had no meaning if the case was after sprinkling.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Always' teaches that a פיגול sprinkling never changes the מעילה status, in either direction.
